briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and DeepSeek R2 intensify AGI benchmark race as compute shortages bite

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs race toward AGI with o4 and R2 releases pushing capabilities while regulatory scrutiny mounts. Funding surges past $11B this quarter amid infrastructure bottlenecks. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI's o4 tops internal benchmarks; Anthropic's Claude 4.5 and Google's Gemini 3.0 follow closely. Meta open-sources Llama 4.1 while xAI's Grok-3 targets real-time reasoning. DeepSeek R2 surprises with efficiency gains.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: New vulnerabilities surface in multi-agent deployments. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for CAN bus and IoT.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA Blackwell ramp hits delays; Microsoft and Google expand data centers in Texas and Arizona. TSMC reports record AI chip orders as sovereign compute initiatives accelerate in EU and Asia.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will open-source models close the capability gap before closed labs reach AGI thresholds by 2027?
